chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Sa'ed Abady quoted Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah, on the authority of Al-Nawfaly, on the authority of Al-Sakoony, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers, on the authority of Ali (peace be upon them) that God's Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Among the signs of misery are: solidity of the eye, hard-heartedness, excessive greed to gain one’s daily bread and insisting on committing sins.

key_terms.جَمُودُ الْعَيْنِ: Solidity or fixedness of the eye (indicating lack of reflection or softness)

ai.seo_question: What are the four signs of misery according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Khisal, Shaykh al-Saduq presents these four signs of misery (al-shaqaw) as the antithesis of felicity, emphasizing the causal link between internal spiritual rigidity and external behavioral manifestations. This narration is often cited in Shia ethical discourse to illustrate how persistent sin hardens the heart, leading to a state of spiritual blindness and insatiable worldly attachment.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-96 Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutevakil - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Sa’ed Abady quoted Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah, on the authority of Al-Nawfaly, on the authority of Al-Sakoony, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of his forefathers (MGB), on the authority of Ali (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “
The following are amongst the signs of misery: solidity of the eye , hard-heartedness, excessive greed to gain one’s daily bread and insisting on committing sins.”
